name: background-image
summary: Background image with an optional colour or gradient filter laid over it.

arguments.name: $image-url
accepts: an image path, as a string; a list, a number, a colour or a boolean is refused
null to filter the element itself instead
var(), url(), image-set() or a gradient, written as they are rather than wrapped in url()
none, the CSS keyword, written as it is rather than as url(none)

arguments.name: $filter-color
accepts: one colour, or several colour stops for a gradient, in the forms the gradient mixin takes
with $image-url null, an image as the overlay layer too: a gradient, url(), image-set() or var()
a word that is not a colour, a quoted colour, a length and a CSS-wide keyword are refused

arguments.name: $filter-direction
accepts: a direction name such as top or bottom-left
an angle in deg, grad, rad or turn, or 0
"to top" or "to left top" as a string
var() or calc()

arguments.name: $size
accepts: cover, the default, contain or auto
a length or a percentage, one or two of them
var(), calc() and the other maths functions
null to leave background-size out

arguments.name: $position
accepts: center center, the default, or any of left, center, right, top and bottom
lengths and percentages, up to the four-value form such as right 10px bottom 20px
var(), calc() and the other maths functions
null to leave background-position out

arguments.name: $repeat
accepts: no-repeat, the default, repeat, repeat-x, repeat-y, space or round
two of them, one per axis, such as repeat space
var()
null to leave background-repeat out

examples: .a { @include background-image("/img/tile.png", null, null, 40px, left top, repeat); }
.a { @include background-image("/img/a.png", rgba(0,0,0,0.5), null, 40px, left top, repeat); }
rejects: .a { @include background-image("/img/a.png", null, null, cover, center center, huge); }
caveats: The filter goes over the image as a second background layer, so a $size, $position or $repeat meant for the photograph would shrink or tile the wash with it. The mixin writes one value per layer instead: measured in Chrome 152, Firefox 156 and Safari 26.6.2, `background-size: cover, 40px` sizes the gradient cover and the image 40px auto, and repeat and position layer the same way.

With $image-url null the filter is an ::after layer over the element, and it carries `pointer-events: none`. Without it the caret could not be put on the element's own text: measured with caretPositionFromPoint, Chrome 152 and Firefox 156 answered with another node and Safari 26.6.2 was unaffected.
The element's direct children are lifted above that layer inside `:where()`, so a rule of the page's own on one of them wins.

With no $image-url and no $filter-color there is nothing to lay over anything: only background-position, background-repeat and background-size are written. Until 4.0.0 an empty ::after covered the element.
$filter-direction turns a gradient, so it is only read when $filter-color has more than one colour; passed with one it warns and is left out.
